verdicts.title: The multi-output `apply` override added by #987 breaks `torch.func.grad` without an enclosing `vmap` for both linear-CE kernels
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced independently on the current tree with the repo venv (torch 2.14.0). packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/kernels/_linear_ce_chunked.py:277-281 overrides `apply` to return `super().apply(*args)[0]`, and :330 unpacks `_, lse, token_weight = output`. Under a bare functorch Grad transform, torch/_functorch/autograd_function.py:124-150 builds `Generated`, whose forward re-enters `custom_function_call` one level down; with no vmap level left that lands on the overridden `apply`, so `Generated.setup_context` receives a single tensor. Instrumenting `setup_context` shows it called twice: once with the real 3-tuple and once with a bare Tensor. Results: `grad(f)` and `grad(f, (0,1))` over `linear_cross_entropy_chunked` raise `ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 3)`; `vmap(grad(...))` and plain `.backward()` both succeed. Confirmed it is a regression: the same probe against `git show a839782e^:.../_linear_ce_chunked.py` gives `OLD grad(0) OK` and `OLD vmap(grad) OK`. Confirmed the user-facing path: `opaque.api.alignment.sft.loss._nll.fused_nll_loss` routes to the chunked kernel on CPU whenever opaque-patches is importable (packages/opaque-alignment/src/opaque/api/alignment/_fused_lce.py:40-62), and `grad(fused_nll_loss)` fails with the same ValueError while `vmap(grad(...))` and `.backward()` pass. Confirmed the consumer: packages/opaque-auditing/src/opaque/api/auditing/attacks/_gradient.py:144 is `grad_fn = torch.func.grad(loss_fn)` with no vmap, called per example at :159, so any fused-LM-head `loss_fn` makes `gradient_scores` raise. Confirmed no test covers bare grad: packages/opaque-patches/tests/kernels/test_linear_ce_chunked.py and test_linear_cross_entropy.py use only `vmap(grad(...))` and `torch.autograd.grad`. One correction to the finding: the failure is not always ValueError. When the per-token loss vector has exactly 3 elements (e.g. seq_len 4), iterating the 1-D tensor satisfies the 3-way unpack with garbage and the failure moves to `TypeError: _ChunkedLinearCE.backward() missing 2 required positional arguments` — still a hard error, never a silent wrong number. The Triton twin (linear_cross_entropy.py:1005-1008 override, :1061 four-way unpack) has the identical shape and the same functorch mechanism, but it is CUDA/Triton-only so I could not execute it; that one link is inferred from code, not run.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: On the current tree, any bare `torch.func.grad` (no enclosing `vmap`) over the fused/chunked linear cross-entropy raises instead of returning a gradient. Reproduced on CPU with the repo venv: `grad(lambda h: linear_cross_entropy_chunked(h, w, labels))(h)` -> `ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 3)`, and `grad(lambda h: fused_nll_loss(h, w, labels))(h)` -> the same, while `vmap(grad(...))` and `loss.backward()` both work. Pre-#987 (a839782e^) bare `grad` worked, so this is a regression introduced by the multi-output `apply` override. The concrete blast radius is `opaque.auditing.gradient_scores`, whose only differentiation path is `grad_fn = torch.func.grad(loss_fn)` (_gradient.py:144): a gradient-norm privacy audit against any model or loss that uses the fused LM-head CE cannot run at all. Failure is always loud (ValueError, or TypeError when the token count happens to be 3 and the tensor unpack accidentally succeeds); no silently wrong gradients, no epsilon impact. The DP-SGD training path (`clipped_grad` -> vmap(grad)) and ordinary `.backward()` are unaffected, which is why CI is green. The Triton CUDA twin carries the identical override and a four-way unpack and is expected to break the same way; that was not executed (no CUDA host).

verdicts.title: `_can_use_native_gqa`'s functorch guard never fires on the DP-SGD transform: `is_batchedtensor` is False under `vmap(grad(...))`
verdicts.reasoning: The predicate claim is true and I verified it directly. packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/transformers/components/attention.py:124 reads `if query.device.type != "cuda" or torch._C._functorch.is_batchedtensor(query): return False`. Probing the three transforms on this torch build: plain `vmap` -> is_batchedtensor True / is_gradtrackingtensor False; `vmap(grad(...))` -> is_batchedtensor **False** / is_gradtrackingtensor True; bare `grad` -> False / True. The DP path is vmap-outside-grad (packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/clipping/_clipped_grad.py uses `grad_and_value`, wrapped by `_vmap` in _clipped_fun.py), so the tensor reaching attention is grad-tracking on the outside and the single-level check misses it. The correct two-level unwrap idiom already exists in the same package (_linear_ce_chunked.py:88-103). No test asserts the negative case; test_attention.py:192-201 is CUDA-marked and uses plain tensors. HOWEVER I have to cut the claimed consequences down substantially. (a) 'SDPAParams reads wrapper geometry / wrong shapes' is refuted: constructing `torch.backends.cuda.SDPAParams` inside `vmap(grad(...))` succeeds and reports the *logical* per-example shape (probe: (2,3,4,4) plain vs (3,4,4) inside the transform), i.e. the geometry it sees is the right one. (b) 'numerics could be wrong' is refuted: `F.scaled_dot_product_attention(..., enable_gqa=True)` under `vmap(grad(...))` agrees bit-for-bit with the repeat_interleave reference for dQ/dK/dV (maxdiff 0.0 in float64), it just emits functorch's 'no batching rule' performance-fallback warning. (c) 'defeating #985's purpose' is unmeasured and plausibly backwards: `_grouped_sdpa` also issues its SDPA calls on the same functorch-wrapped tensors, so it takes the same fallback loop once per KV head, i.e. more fallback launches than the native call. So what remains is a genuine dead guard whose only established consequence is that the branch the author meant to exclude is taken; no correctness or privacy impact, and the perf direction is unverified (no CUDA host here).
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: On CUDA, a DP-SGD step under `vmap(grad(...))` reaches `_can_use_native_gqa` with a GradTrackingTensor, for which `torch._C._functorch.is_batchedtensor` returns False (verified on this torch build), so the guard added by #985 does not fire and the native `enable_gqa=True` SDPA branch runs inside the transform instead of `_grouped_sdpa`. Established consequence: none beyond branch selection. `SDPAParams` built from the wrapper reports the correct logical per-example geometry, and `enable_gqa=True` under `vmap(grad(...))` produces gradients identical to the explicit head-replication reference (maxdiff 0.0, float64), taking functorch's per-sample batching fallback. So this is a guard that silently does nothing on the DP transform (it still works under plain `vmap`, where is_batchedtensor is True) — a code-hygiene/perf-intent defect, not a numerical or privacy defect. Whether the native branch is faster or slower than `_grouped_sdpa` under the fallback was not measured (no CUDA device available).

verdicts.title: RMSNorm / fused-add-RMSNorm / RoPE backwards overwrite the upstream gradient buffer on a single backward, not only on a repeated one (wider than tracked #898)
verdicts.reasoning: The static aliasing is exactly as described and I re-read every cited line: rms_norm.py:533 `dY = dY.contiguous().view(-1, dim)` then :557 `dX = dY if in_place else torch.zeros_like(dY)`, with dX handed to the kernel as the output pointer (:562-565); fused_add_rms_norm.py:322 the same with `torch.empty_like`; rope_embedding.py:236-238 and :262-266 pass `dQ` as both in and out pointer, and :455-458 likewise for dQ_out/dK_out, with no `in_place` flag at all. `Opaque_RMSNorm.backward` (rms_norm.py:740-742) does `go = grad_output.contiguous()` then `go2 = go.reshape(-1, dim)`, so for an already-contiguous incoming grad `go2` shares storage with the engine-supplied gradient. components/rms_norm.py:35,41 do pass `in_place_bwd=True` for the default llama and gemma RMSNorm patches (gemma2/olmo2/glm4 variants pass False), and the public `opaque_rms_norm` defaults to `in_place_backward=False`. I verified the autograd-engine link with a CPU stand-in Function whose backward writes into its `grad_output`: after `torch.autograd.grad(y, x, grad_outputs=g)` the caller's `g` is observably mutated (3.0 -> 6.0), and in a shared-grad topology (`out = a + F.apply(a)`, where AddBackward hands the *same* tensor to both edges) the sibling branch's gradient comes out wrong (4.0 instead of 3.0). What I could NOT establish: (1) the Triton kernels are CUDA-only and this host has no CUDA, so the actual buffer overwrite was not executed; (2) I looked for an in-model topology among the affected families that would hit the shared-grad case and did not find one — Llama/Gemma use these norms as pre-norms whose incoming gradient is freshly allocated by the consumer projections (or accumulated across q/k/v and gate/up), and the families with a post-attention norm before the residual add (Gemma2, OLMo2, GLM4, Cohere2) are the ones configured with `in_place_bwd=False`. So the harm needs direct kernel use with an explicit `grad_outputs` that the caller then reuses, on CUDA. Tracking: this duplicates open issue #898, whose scope is recorded in this repo's own audit notes as 'the wider sweep across the other fused kernels (rope_embedding, rms_norm, fused_add_rms_norm, moe, Opaque_LoRA_QKV, Opaque_LoRA_W)' for exactly this backward-buffer-overwrite class; the first-vs-repeated distinction is a refinement to add to #898, not a separate defect.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: On CUDA with the Triton kernels, `Opaque_RMSNorm.backward` with `in_place_bwd=True` (the default for the llama and gemma RMSNorm component patches) passes the engine-supplied gradient tensor to the Triton kernel as both input and output pointer, and `_RoPEBackward` / `_RoPE_QK_Backward` do the same unconditionally. If such a node is the first node the autograd engine visits for a user-supplied `grad_outputs` — i.e. direct kernel use such as `torch.autograd.grad(opaque_rms_norm(x, w), x, grad_outputs=g)` — the caller's `g` is overwritten in place; the write goes through Triton so no version counter is bumped and autograd raises nothing. Verified on CPU with an equivalent stand-in Function that the engine does hand the caller's tensor through and that it is observably mutated, and that a shared-grad topology yields a wrong sibling gradient; the Triton overwrite itself was not executed (no CUDA host). I found no path inside the supported patched model families that reaches the shared/aliased-gradient case, because the families whose decoder layer puts a norm directly under the residual add are configured with `in_place_bwd=False`. So the practical exposure is direct kernel callers on CUDA that reuse their seed gradient, not DPTrainer or `clipped_grad` (scalar loss -> engine-created ones tensor). Same defect class as open issue #898.

verdicts.title: Generic fused LoRA QKV wrapper applies RoPE on Cohere2's NoPE (full-attention) layers
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced independently. Upstream transformers 5.15.1 .venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/transformers/models/cohere2/modeling_cohere2.py:196 sets `self.sliding_window = config.sliding_window if config.layer_types[layer_idx] == 'sliding_attention' else None` and :226-228 applies rotary only `if self.sliding_window is not None` — the full-attention layers are deliberately NoPE. packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/peft/components/qkv.py:25 keeps 'Cohere2Attention' in `_FUSEABLE_QKV_ATTENTION_CLASSES`, :43-44 routes it to the generic `_make_fused_qkv_attention_forward`, and :127-133 calls `apply_rotary_pos_emb(query_states, key_states, cos, sin)` with no guard. I built a 4-layer Cohere2 with layer_types ['sliding_attention','full_attention','sliding_attention','full_attention'], installed a reference `_opaque_fused_qkv` (plain projections, the same technique tests/peft/test_gemma3_fused_lora_qkv.py:126-139 uses) and forced the CUDA branch by patching `torch.Tensor.is_cuda`: per-layer self_attn output vs the unpatched forward gives maxdiff 0.0 on both sliding layers and 1.9e-04 (1.24% rel) / 1.3e-04 (0.84% rel) on the two full-attention layers. Only the NoPE layers diverge, which isolates the cause to the unconditional rotary call. Reachability verified: `apply_model_patches` has `peft: bool = True` (packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/__init__.py:25), `_auto_fuse_lora` installs the wrapper whenever q/k/v all carry LoRA with frozen bias and no lora_dropout (peft/_router.py:74-97; PEFT's default lora_dropout is 0.0), and `_lora_patching_allowed` does not block it. The wrapper delegates to the original forward only when `not hidden_states.is_cuda` (qkv.py:106), so the bug fires exactly on the GPU training path. No sibling guard exists: transformers/models/cohere2.py installs only MLP/causal-LM patches (rms_norm_kind=None, fused_add_rms_kind=None) and never replaces Cohere2Attention.forward, so upstream's guard is live until the peft wrapper displaces it. Test-gap claim verified: Cohere2Config(num_hidden_layers=1).layer_types == ['sliding_attention'], and the only Cohere2 fused-LoRA test (tests/peft/test_fused_lora_parallel_residual.py:47-53, :127-131) uses num_hidden_layers=1, so a full-attention layer is never instantiated. Default Cohere2Config (40 layers) makes every 4th layer full_attention, so 25% of layers are affected. Severity lowered from critical to high: it is silent numerical divergence at default patch settings for a documented supported family, but it needs a specific model family plus LoRA on all of q/k/v plus CUDA, and it has no epsilon/privacy effect (affects_epsilon false).
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: Load a Cohere2 model (default config: layer_types repeat 3x sliding_attention + 1x full_attention, so 10 of 40 layers are NoPE), wrap it with a LoraConfig targeting q_proj/k_proj/v_proj, call `opaque.patches.apply_model_patches(model)` (peft fusion is on by default) and train on CUDA. `_auto_fuse_lora` replaces every Cohere2Attention.forward with the generic fused wrapper, which applies `apply_rotary_pos_emb` unconditionally, whereas upstream applies it only on sliding-window layers. Every full-attention layer therefore computes attention on RoPE-rotated Q/K although the architecture defines it as NoPE: forward, loss and per-sample gradients are wrong for 25% of layers and nothing warns or raises. Verified device-independently by forcing the CUDA branch on a 4-layer Cohere2: sliding layers match upstream exactly (maxdiff 0.0) while both full-attention layers diverge (1.9e-04 / 1.3e-04 max abs, 1.24% / 0.84% relative on randomly initialised weights). CPU runs are unaffected because the wrapper delegates to the original forward when the input is not CUDA, and the only existing Cohere2 fused-LoRA test uses num_hidden_layers=1, whose single layer is sliding_attention, so no test instantiates the broken case. No privacy/epsilon impact; the defect is silent numerical infidelity to the loaded architecture.
